date_policy: Dates identify the declared run, report, commit or chat event. Date basis is retained per entry; file modification time is not treated as a run date.

records.name: Historical optical sequential reference audit: T=2 passes and T=8 fails the peak grid gate
records.date_basis: Dated public review in project chat Plan 3D Dysthe equation model, turn 01a0b0a9-0861-7b43-8c82-24ee257450d7 (America/New_York). This is the review date, not a separately recorded simulation start timestamp.
records.model: Dysthe3D-1.27: historical three-coordinate optical equation, periodic domain of side lengths 12, full cubic nonlinearity and derivative correction
records.status: Failed sampled peak grid-convergence screen at T=8; sequence stopped after T=2 passed
findings: The retained sequence-summary.json has two stages: T=2 with status pass and T=8 with status fail and return code 2.
At T=8, the largest sampled peak discrepancy between nested grids is 0.00795352933 (0.79535%), exceeding the 0.005 (0.5%) gate. The common-grid relative L2 discrepancy is 2.50306424e-6.
Fine-grid time refinement gives maximum relative L2 discrepancy 5.54161170e-12 and peak discrepancy 1.04007004e-11. These small discrepancies do not cancel the failed peak grid screen.

The retained implementation uses a NumPy Fourier integrating-factor RK4 reference. Its configuration contains neural training and CUDA fields, but this reference calculation does not instantiate a neural network.
limitations: Accuracy of the continuous spatial supremum is unresolved. The peak comparison samples each grid separately; it is not a certified continuum maximum.
This is a fixed periodic domain. No domain-enlargement test, whole-space decay conclusion, global-existence theorem, or blowup finding follows.
This optical model is preserved as research history and is not evidence for the active water-wave-dysthe-spatial-v1 baseline. Passing a reference screen would not establish PINN accuracy.

records.name: Historical optical fine-step trajectory to T=2048 and descriptive local oscillation fit
records.date_basis: The retained report.tex is dated 18 September 2026; the public review turn 01a0b558-b1ba-7192-8bc4-6a1df4d36778 has the same local date. This dates the report/review, not an independently logged start timestamp.
records.model: Dysthe3D-1.27: historical three-coordinate optical equation, periodic cube of side length 12; amplitude 0.3 cosine-power packet
records.kind: Exploratory long-time numerical trajectory and diagnostic report
findings: The trajectory integrates from t=0 to 2048 on a 64^3 grid with dt=0.01, 204800 steps, and 257 saved frames in the observation window [1024,2048]. It does not reset the initial packet at t=1024.
The retained summary reports 18421.4701 seconds (5.1171 hours), maximum relative mass drift 7.39085032e-12, and maximum retained spectral-edge fraction 3.27698233e-18.

Across integer diagnostic times in [1024,2048], the sampled peak ranges from 0.07376859 to 0.23707285, with mean 0.13071707. The fitted late log-log slope has R^2=0.0035077, so these samples do not support a useful single power-law decay fit.

A separate local four-harmonic descriptive fit on [1536,1664] uses 129 samples, a fitted base period 11.48213, RMSE 0.00513424, and R^2=0.9849756. Withheld points selected the harmonic count before refitting all points.
The original implementation is NumPy CPU reference integration. CUDA and network configuration entries are retained provenance; this run supplies no new long-time PINN prediction.
limitations: Long-time field and peak accuracy remain unresolved: the saved qualification explicitly records no grid/time refinement and unknown accumulated error before the observation window. Small mass drift is not a field-error bound.
The harmonic fit is local description, not an independent test, a future-time forecast, a new PDE solution, or proof of a breather, soliton, recurrence, or asymptotic law.
Periodic confinement and a mass-dependent lower bound obstruct interpreting the ordinary maximum as whole-space decay to zero. This historical optical trajectory is not active water-wave evidence.
Production field/checkpoint arrays are not present in the inspected results directory; the archive preserves diagnostic summaries and code, rather than claiming full raw-field reproducibility.

records.name: Historical optical coarse breathing preview: T=12288 target stopped at t=10321
records.date_basis: Dated public review turn 01a0b5c4-c0f4-70d3-851e-023e1d95bfe1 and the retained 18 September 2026 report. The run summary contains elapsed duration but no wall-clock start date.
records.model: Dysthe3D-1.27: historical three-coordinate optical equation, periodic cube of side length 12; separate 32^3 coarse-grid preview
records.status: failed_diagnostics; stopped at t=10321 before target T=12288
records.kind: Exploratory long-time preview with an operational diagnostic stop
findings: The separate preview uses dt=0.5 and 32^3 points, starts from t=0, targets T=12288, and records a detailed [1500,2500] observation window plus showcase windows.
The retained summary reports 20642 steps, 726 saved frames, and 121.2381 seconds before stopping at t=10321. It leaves 3934 planned steps uncompleted.
Maximum relative mass drift reaches 0.00100007306 (0.1000073%), exceeding the 0.001 stop threshold. Maximum recorded spectral-edge fraction is 2.65134688e-6.

The retained focus-window statistics report peak values from 0.07372305 to 0.23691754 and effective-volume values from 164.36659 to 924.40993, with peak-volume correlation -0.9134428. These describe oscillatory concentration in the preview.
The report records at most 1.04% sampled-peak disagreement with the earlier fine-step run at common integer times 1500 through 2048. This comparison changes the grid and time step together.
limitations: The operational mass-drift stop is a numerical diagnostic failure, not evidence of PDE blowup or loss of solution existence.
Long-time field accuracy is unresolved, particularly beyond t=2048. The overlap check does not separate spatial and temporal errors or validate the complex field.
Breathing-like concentration diagnostics do not establish a localized breather or soliton, and the trajectory is not a long-time PINN result.
This is historical optical evidence on a periodic domain, not the active water-wave model or a whole-space decay test. Production frame arrays are not present in the inspected results directory.

chat_review.title: Plan 3D Dysthe equation model
chat_review.date_basis: Latest completed public turn returned by read_thread; individual message timestamps are unavailable.
chat_review.category: Historical numerical PDE, scientific visualization and optical PINN research
topics: Equation 1.27 versus printed 1.32 sign audit and Fourier symbols
Fractionally weighted dispersive estimates, scaling and finite-time peak searches
Non-Gaussian/random inputs, restricted spectra and cancellation
Nonlinear traveling profiles, collisions and optical stripe perturbations
Envelope/phase/carrier figures, animation and interpretation corrections
Optical PINN implementation, A100 smoke/training/evaluation, Slurm support
Periodic long-horizon reference runs, oscillatory fits and breathing hypothesis
One accidentally pasted TDA pruning review, explicitly withdrawn as wrong chat
chat_review.summary: The chat developed a historical numerical programme from exact linear propagation and weighted-decay studies into nonlinear profile experiments and one-input optical PINN validation. It produced multiple reports and visualizations, then reviewed long periodic reference trajectories. The final discussion emphasizes formulation fidelity, finite-time evidence, per-input retraining and the limits of peak/loss-only claims.
results: Canonical Gaussian weighted peak searches reached t = 1024; restricted-input studies completed 40 screened records after retained follow-ups. (Recorded historical CPU numerical evidence; no theorem or counterexample.)

28 discrete spatial Dysthe traveling profiles and refined collision/perturbation tests were reported; optical stripe perturbations were resolved through t = 4 but later t = 8 remained unresolved. (Different nonlinear formulations explicitly separated.)

The original 90-degree two-packet pair has zero intensity cross-term under the real-coefficient canonical propagator; an in-phase control demonstrates interference. (Interpretation correction preserved alongside earlier figures.)

One optical PINN completed 20,000 A100 steps; independent short-time evaluation reports 0.665 percent maximum relative complex-field error over 0 <= t <= 0.5. (One input/seed benchmark; not generalization or a long-time result.)

An optical reference run reached t = 8 but its sampled peak-grid discrepancy 0.795 percent exceeded the 0.5 percent gate although field/time checks passed. (Reference peak-resolution failure; not PINN-training failure.)

A periodic optical fine-step run reached t = 2048 in about 5.12 h with maximum relative mass drift 7.39e-12; long-time grid/time accuracy was not validated. (Completed reference trajectory, accuracy unresolved.)
A separate coarse optical preview targeting t = 12288 stopped at t = 10321 after relative mass drift exceeded 0.1 percent. (Stopped diagnostic-limited preview; not blow-up or completed target.)
Local four-harmonic fit on 1536 <= t <= 1664 has recorded R2 about 0.985 and base period 11.48. (Descriptive local fit; no future prediction, decay law or proof of breather.)
unresolved: No new uniform decay theorem or certified counterexample.
Long optical trajectories lack independent late-time grid/time refinement; mass conservation alone does not validate them.
Breathing-like peak modulation does not establish a localized breather without spatial/phase evidence.
The trained historical PINN fits one prescribed input and requires retraining for changed initial data.
No calibrated measured-data propagation benchmark was completed.
